simple.meaning: חָבַק (châbaq) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to clasp (the hands or in embrace).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 13 times across Genesis, 2 Kings, Job, Proverbs, Ecclesiastes, and 2 more, beginning at Genesis 29:13. Its contexts include family, family line, mountain, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חָבַק (H2263).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: חָבַק (châbaq) / H2263 is traced through Genesis 29:13, Genesis 33:4, Genesis 48:10, 2 Kings 4:16 as a generated source-based concept entry.

structuredEvidence.definition: to clasp (the hands or in embrace)

firstOccurrence.englishText: When Laban heard the news of Jacob, his sister’s son, he ran to meet Jacob, and embraced him, and kissed him, and brought him to his house. Jacob told Laban all these things.

timeline.evidenceText: When Laban heard the news of Jacob, his sister’s son, he ran to meet Jacob, and embraced him, and kissed him, and brought him to his house. Jacob told Laban all these things.
Esau ran to meet him, embraced him, fell on his neck, kissed him, and they wept.
Now the eyes of Israel were dim for age, so that he couldn’t see well. Joseph brought them near to him; and he kissed them, and embraced them.
He said, “At this season, when the time comes around, you will embrace a son.”
They are wet with the showers of the mountains,
Esteem her, and she will exalt you.
For why should you, my son, be captivated with an adulteress?

definitions.short: to clasp (the hands or in embrace)
definitions.full: H2263. chabaq [ חָבַק ] verb clasp, embrace (Late Hebrew id. ; חַבֵּק ᵑ7 ; Mandean , NSyriac ; Arabic II. collect one's possessions, etc., Frey) — Qal Infinitive לַחֲבוֺק Eccl 3:5 ; Participle חֹבֵּק 4:5 ; חֹבֶקֶת 2Kin 4:16 ; — embrace , with accusative בֵּן 4:16 ; יָדָיו Eccl 4:5 (said of הַכְּסִיל = fold his arms, i.e. be idle; compare חִבֻּק ); no object expressed 3:5 (|| Pi`el ). Pi`el Perfect חִבְּקוּ Job 24:8 ; Lam 4:5 ; Imperfect וַיְחַבֵּק Gen 48:10 ; וַיְחַבֶּקֿ 29:13 ; וַיְחַבְּקֵהוּ 33:4 ; 3 feminine singular suffix תְּחַבְּקֵ֫נִי Song 2:6 ; 8:3 ; 2 masculine singular וּתְחַבֵּק Prov 5:20 , suffix תְּחַבְּקֶ֫נָּה 4:8 ; Infinitive חַבֵּק Eccl 3:5 ; — embrace of person, no object מֵחַבֵּק לִרְחֹק עת 3:5 (|| Qal ); followed by לְ Gen 29:13 (J), 48:10 (E); followed by suffix 33:4 (J), Prov 4:8 ; Song 2:6 ; 8:3 ; with accusative Prov 5:20 ; embrace צוּר for want of shelter Job 24:8 (of poor); embrace refuse-heaps אשׁפתות Lam 4:5 , i.e. are outcasts.
